title: SpaceX Proposes $50B Data Center in Cochise Arizona

tickers.name: Space Exploration Technologies Corp. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The aerospace company is planning a new computing facility in Cochise, Arizona, that would generate between $30 million and $100 million in new annual property tax revenue for the county. The proposed site would consist of nine buildings with a total power capacity of approximately 6 GW, representing a total projected investment of $50 billion.

The project includes a proposal for SpaceX to pay for $3.6 billion in new power lines to be given to the local co-op without the utility taking on debt. Riley Trettel, who leads energy and data center development for the company, said the facility would not use on-site power generation or industrial water, and claimed the project could reduce residential electricity bills for Sulphur Springs members by up to 40%.

selectedTweets.text:
Riley Trettel (Energy & Data Center Development at SpaceX) in yesterdays Cochise Data Center meeting. 

He claims the project will deliver up to:
- 40% off residential power bills for Sulphur Springs members, for the life of the project
- $53 million a year to the SSVEC Foundation, for education and the community
- $190 million a year in extra capital for Sulphur Springs, for projects or back to members
- $200 million a year for AEPCO and its members. About $100 million of that for Sulphur Springs
- $3.6 billion in new power lines, paid by SpaceX and given to the co-op. The co-op takes on no debt
- $30 to $100 million a year in new property tax, and a 20% cut in everyone else's county property taxes
- $250 million, one time, in sales tax. He said it could pay off the jail bond and fund the sheriff, fire districts, and the hospital
- $50 billion invested in the project
- 1,000 permanent jobs and 5,000 construction jobs
- No industrial water. Water for staff and maintenance about equal to 20–30 homes a year
- No gas turbines and no power plant on the site. The computers buy power from the co-op grid
- Dark-sky lighting, pointed at the ground
- Cooling equipment more than 1,500 feet from any neighboring property line or public road

This project is clearly extremely positive for the area.
